active_projects.description: Research algebraic methods for establishing a Jónsson-Tarski-style representation theorem for the bimodal logic TM with primitives Since (S), Until (U), and Box (□), plus material implication (→) and bottom (⊥) as the primitive Boolean operators. The goal is to determine whether the Lindenbaum-Tarski algebra of TM forms a variety of Boolean algebras with operators (BAOs) that admits a concrete representation into complex algebras of relational structures (task frames). Key questions: (1) Since S and U are binary normal operators, does the standard Jónsson-Tarski representation for n-ary BAOs apply directly, or does the interaction with the S5 modal operator □ introduce complications? (2) What role does orthodox axiomatizability (no IRR rule) play — per Venema 1993 (Anti-Axioms), orthodox systems ensure closure under ultraproducts, but TM uses the IRR rule in the ConservativeExtension module; does this affect the algebraic representation? (3) Can the existing TenseS5Algebra.lean structure be extended to a full BAO with S/U operators, and does the Lindenbaum quotient construction yield a representable algebra? (4) What is the relationship between the parametric representation theorem (ParametricRepresentation.lean) and a Jónsson-Tarski-style algebraic representation — are they equivalent, or does one subsume the other? (5) How do the Prior-UZ/SZ axioms (discrete well-ordering) and the uniformity axioms (ordered abelian group structure) interact with the algebraic representation? Literature base: Venema 1991 (dissertation Ch2 + App A), Venema 1993 (Anti-Axioms), Goldblatt-Hodkinson-Venema 2003, Venema 1997 (Atom Structures), de Rijke-Venema 1995 (Sahlqvist for BAOs), Blackburn-de Rijke-Venema 2001 Ch5 (not yet obtained). All papers are in literature/ with markdown conversions.

active_projects.description: Redesign the FMP filtration for strict temporal semantics. The 2 sorry theorems in Decidability/FMP/TruthPreservation.lean — mcs_all_future_closure (line 263) and mcs_all_past_closure (line 281) — are deprecated because the temporal T-axiom (Gphi -> phi) is NOT valid under strict semantics. filtration_all_future_forward and filtration_all_past_forward depend on them. The FMP module is separate from the main decidability pipeline (decide is sorry-free), but completing it formally proves the finite model property. Resolution options: (A) restrict FMP statement to serial frames where temporal seriality holds, (B) redesign filtration to avoid temporal reflexivity entirely, (C) prove the filtered model satisfies a weaker correctness property sufficient for the FMP theorem. Note: mcs_finite_model_property in FMP.lean does NOT directly use these sorry lemmas, so the impact is localized to filtration_all_future_forward/backward.

active_projects.description: Add a .claude/rules/ rule enforcing plan compliance for implementation agents. Root cause: lean-implementation-agent invented a theorems-as-interval shortcut for task 107 Phase 1 instead of following the planned Burgess D0 seed construction. The agent definition, skill, and workflow docs tell agents HOW to execute (lean_goal, phase markers, builds) but never say they MUST follow the plan approach.
